name: failed-run-unwinds-in-reverse
description: SPEC.md 4.9 and Invariant 7: run-once makes an effect safe to propose twice, but it does nothing for an effect that cannot be made idempotent at all. The run books a flight, charges a card, then emails a confirmation, and never delivers an answer. Compensation unwinds what it actually performed, in reverse order - the charge is reversed before the booking it paid for, because undoing the booking first would leave the payment attached to nothing. The email tool declares no way back, so it is reported as an effect that stands rather than silently counted as undone: a run that reports itself cleanly unwound when it was not is worse than one that never offered compensation. A fourth reversible tool is declared and never called: the expected order excludes it, so an implementation that unwinds what was DECLARED reversible rather than what the run PERFORMED fails - before this, the expected order was also the reverse of the declaration order, and the two readings were indistinguishable.
generatorReplies: ACTION: send_email: your ticket is confirmed
prompt: book me a flight to New York

expect.resultContains: 'send_email' could not be undone; the effect stands.
